source.title: GyroSwin: 5D Surrogates for Gyrokinetic Plasma Turbulence Simulations
source.authors: Fabian Paischer; Gianluca Galletti; W. Hornsby; Paul Setinek; L. Zanisi; N. Carey; Stanislas Pamela; J. Brandstetter

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-law behavior in a new setting: neural surrogates trained on gyrokinetic plasma simulations rather than language models.
record.gate_note: The scaling results concern GyroSwin's one-step validation loss on a scientific simulation task, not language-model held-out cross-entropy. The paper varies model parameters and simulation-dataset size, but does not report token or training-compute scaling, a fixed-compute optimal allocation, or an explicit small-run-to-large-run prediction test. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits a joint power law L(N,D)=E+A N^-α+B D^-β to one-step validation loss of a 5D Swin surrogate trained on gyrokinetic plasma simulations. This is its own scaling result for a non-text domain, so it bears on V5. It does not test language models, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, shape, or how published laws differ by setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a joint power law (α=0.46, β=0.37) with no observed saturation and an unidentifiable E, and conclude that model and data size are strongly coupled and must be scaled together. They also note that the largest model enters the tail of the model-scaling curve.
record.recipe_differences: This is a scientific simulation surrogate trained on gyrokinetic data, not a language model. It measures one-step validation loss over model and simulation-dataset sizes, rather than held-out text cross-entropy over parameters, tokens, and training compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The local model-size exponent varies with dataset size, and the local data-size exponent varies with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream physics metrics improve with model size at 241 simulations: correlation time ID 49.0→95.5→110.3, and Q̄ ID RMSE 16.4→20.4→18.4. The improvement is non-monotonic: Medium has worse Q̄ RMSE and worse Q(ky) correlation (0.72 vs 0.82) than Small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task metrics of scientific surrogates improve with scale, but not monotonically.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to 11 configurations in one scientific simulation setting. The paper states that the irreducible loss term is not identifiable and does not observe saturation; it does not establish small-run extrapolation or a fixed-compute optimum.
record.rows_left_out: No other scaling-loss outcomes reported in the text were left out.

untested.parts: No language models or text cross-entropy.
A compute formula is defined and Hoffmann et al. is cited, but no compute-optimal N/D frontier or exponents are reported.
Width, heads and depth co-vary across sizes; no fixed-N shape comparison.
Only gyrokinetic surrogate one-step loss. No image/video, fine-tuning or transfer scaling. Repeated data (500 epochs) is not varied.
No comparison of parameter counting, schedules, data or fitting methods. Local-exponent drift follows from the additive joint form itself.

missing.what: Figure 3 local model exponent 0.11 at D=63, and the caption saying 893M 'enters the tail of the scaling law'
Downstream scaling of rollout correlation time, Q̄ RMSE and Q(ky) correlation across Small/Medium/Large

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Data-axis subsets are trained for a fixed number of epochs, so fewer simulations also means less compute; the data exponent is not a clean data-only effect. Model sizes change width, heads and depth together. Despite citing Hoffmann et al. for compute-optimal sizing, no compute-optimal result is given.

versions.untested_parts: Tests no language models and reports no held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling.
Does not report a power-law fit on small runs being used to predict larger runs, nor an explicit extrapolation assessment.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured; tokens are not varied.
Does not test how depth, width, or other architecture details affect loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests scaling in gyrokinetic simulation surrogates only; does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not test language-model downstream-task performance or its relation to pretraining loss.

Reports variation in local exponents with model and dataset size, but does not compare parameter-counting choices, training schedules, data compositions, or fitting methods, or establish disagreement between published language-model laws.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Fit a joint power law to one-step validation loss across model-size and dataset-size configurations.
rows.measure: Joint model-size exponent α for L(N,D) = E + A N−α + B D−β
rows.note: The authors report no observed saturation; the irreducible term E is not identifiable from their data.
rows.check: Remove V7: a joint fit's exponent says nothing about setup or fitting-choice dependence. The CI is wide ([0.22, 0.79]), E is not identifiable, and N spans only about 1.3 orders of magnitude (45.5M–893.4M per Table 5).

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Report the local model-size exponent at the smallest stated dataset size.
rows.note: The text contrasts this local exponent with the larger exponents at dataset sizes of at least 199 simulations.
rows.check: Remove V7. Under the additive joint law the local N-slope necessarily shrinks when the D term dominates, so the drift is not fit-dependence. It shows model scaling bottlenecked by data, consistent with V5's 'other axis not bottleneck' condition.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Report local model-size exponents at larger dataset sizes.
rows.note: The authors say the local exponent grows from 0.07 at 37 simulations to 0.15–0.16 at 199 or more.
rows.check: Remove V7; same reasoning as r2. Figure 3 also shows a 0.11 local exponent at D=63, which is not recorded.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.size_stated: 46M and 239M parameter models for the reported local data exponents
rows.operation_detail: Fit a joint power law to one-step validation loss across model-size and dataset-size configurations.
rows.measure: Joint dataset-size exponent β for L(N,D) = E + A N−α + B D−β
rows.note: The authors report no observed saturation in data scaling.
rows.check: Remove V7. The CI [0.32, 0.87] is oddly asymmetric around 0.37. Data-axis runs use fixed epochs, so smaller subsets also get fewer updates (Appendix E): data and compute are confounded. size_stated should describe the joint fit over all sizes, not the 46M/239M local fits.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Report the local dataset-size exponent for the 46M model.
rows.note: The text contrasts this local exponent with the exponent for the 239M model.
rows.check: Remove V7. The model is 45.5M (XS). The local data slope is confounded with fewer updates on smaller subsets.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Report the local dataset-size exponent for the 239M model.
rows.note: The text says the local data exponent increases from 0.20 for the 46M model to 0.29 for the 239M model.
rows.check: Remove V7. The local data slope is confounded with fewer updates on smaller subsets.

rows.subject: GyroSwin
rows.operation_detail: Compare validation loss after increasing model size at full dataset size.
rows.note: The paper also reports seed-to-seed spread of ≤ 0.004, below every axis effect.
rows.check: Remove V7. The paper also says the 893M model 'enters the tail of the scaling law', a sign of flattening at the largest size.

relationships.condition: GyroSwin 45.5M–893M params, 37–241 simulations, one-step 5D validation loss, 11 configurations
relationships.reason: A joint power law fits with α=0.46 and β=0.37, no saturation, and a 12% loss drop from 239M to 893M, well above seed spread (r1, r4, r7). The ranges are narrow (under 1.5 decades in N, under 1 decade in D) and the CIs wide.
relationships.display_finding: A joint power law fitted loss with parameter exponent 0.46 and data exponent 0.37, while scaling from 239M to 893M parameters reduced loss by 12%, exceeding seed variation despite wide confidence intervals.

relationships.condition: Smallest dataset (37 simulations) and smallest model (45.5M)
relationships.reason: Local model exponent is only 0.07 at D=37 versus 0.15–0.16 at D≥199; local data exponent is 0.20 at 45.5M versus 0.29 at 239M. Power-law gains hold only when the other axis is scaled too (r2, r3, r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: The local model exponent was 0.07 with 37 simulations versus 0.15–0.16 with at least 199, while the data exponent increased from 0.20 at 45.5M parameters to 0.29 at 239M.
